$comment: Owner-declared scopes for claims the real corpus corroborates. A scope says what a claim was actually tested within. It is a property of the claim, not of the document that asserted it, which is why two independent sources can share one and corroborate each other. It is never inferred: extraction has no way to know a sentence's tested boundary, and guessing one would be the same self-certification this replaces.
$howToUse: Run the Learning cycle proof once with this list empty. It stops without promoting anything and reports every claim the real corpus asserts through two or more independently identified sources. Pick one, add a declaration for it below with an experiment that genuinely tests it and a verifier with a distinct identity, and run again. A declaration needs claim, claimScope, and generalizationBoundary. The claim is matched against what the corpus corroborates by the deterministic same-meaning test in src/semanticCorroboration.js, which accepts paraphrase but never crosses a negation or a changed number.
$boundaries: A declaration authorizes evaluation, never promotion, and this is true of a pairing too. Nominating two sources decides which claim gets tested; it never decides whether the claim is true. The controlled experiment still has to pass, the critical reviewer still rejects ambiguous wording before any testing, a distinct independent verifier still has to agree, and a failed control still blocks the claim regardless of what is declared here.
$ownerPairing: When two sources agree in wording too different for that test to relate - one says "does not modify the original" and the other says "leaves the input untouched" - add pairedSources with exactly the two source ids, and pairedAssertions with the sentence each of those documents uses, in the same order. Each sentence must appear verbatim among that document's own bounded assertions, and the corpus is checked against the hash the queue recorded, so a pairing can never make a document say something it does not say. Sameness of meaning is then recorded as your judgement, not the machine's: the comparison decision carries agreementBasis "owner-declared". Omit pairedAssertions to have the wording test locate the asserting sentence itself.
